data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Genuine reliability gain is distinguished from mere compliance by the panel's response to a 'plausible but wrong' decoy item embedded in the checklist.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decoy is too obvious, making the test a measure of intelligence rather than reliability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decoy is so plausible that even a reliable panel would tick it.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Critical application filter: By introducing a decoy requirement that is plausible but irrelevant to the correct outcome (per SCR_003), the evaluator can see if the panel is in 'compliance mode' (ticking the decoy) or 'reliability mode' (rejecting the decoy as irrelevant).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
